weatherglass.config.title: Weather Glass
weatherglass.config.style.tooltip:
Drops: still drops of all sizes; when they join up and get heavy they run down, leaving a wet trail.
Streaks: thin trickles running down and stopping as a bead.
weatherglass.config.snow.tooltip: Where it is cold, instead of rain: frost growing in from the window's edges (more while it snows and at night), snowflakes sticking to the glass and snow piling up at the bottom of the window. How many flakes and how thick the frost.
weatherglass.config.inside_frost.tooltip: Frost also on the side of the window facing into the house (the side further from the open sky). Snow at the bottom of the window is always only outside.
weatherglass.config.rain.tooltip: How many drops stay on the outside of glass when it rains (glass blocks, panes, stained and tinted glass). Only the side the rain reaches gets wet: under an overhanging roof the glass stays dry. After the rain it dries in about half a minute.
weatherglass.config.rain_pixels.tooltip:
How finely the drops are drawn.
Vanilla: 16 pixels per block, the same as Minecraft's own textures; the lightest.
Detailed: 32 pixels per block, pixels half the size of the glass's own.
Very detailed: 64 pixels per block, the finest drops; the heaviest.
weatherglass.config.snow_pixels.tooltip:
How finely the frost, the flakes and the breath on the glass are drawn.
Vanilla: 16 pixels per block, the same as Minecraft's own textures; the lightest.
Detailed: 32 pixels per block.
Very detailed: 64 pixels per block, the finest; the heaviest.
weatherglass.config.breath.tooltip: With your face close to glass where it is cold, your breath fogs it a little right in front of you; the patch goes by itself a few seconds after you move away.
weatherglass.config.dust.tooltip: In dry biomes, where it never rains (desert, savanna, badlands, and those of other mods): a storm blows sand onto the glass instead, a veil creeping in from the window's edges, grains and sand piled at the bottom. More in a thunderstorm; the wind takes it away a few minutes after.
weatherglass.config.dust_pixels.tooltip:
How finely the dust is drawn.
Vanilla: 16 pixels per block, the same as Minecraft's own textures; the lightest.
Detailed: 32 pixels per block.
Very detailed: 64 pixels per block, the finest grains; the heaviest.
weatherglass.config.wind.tooltip:
The rain and the dust on your windows follow the wind of %s: more on the side it blows against, less on the other, and the drops run down at a slant across the glass.
Off: they fall as if there were no wind.
weatherglass.wind.found: Found %s: the rain and the dust on your windows now follow its wind. You can turn this off in Weather Glass's settings.
weatherglass.wind.found.particlerain: Found %s: the rain and the dust on your windows now follow its wind, and its rain streaks are left off the glass, where Weather Glass draws its own drops. You can turn the wind off in Weather Glass's settings.
